title: Chariot-1 AI models launched by MeitY under IndiaAI Mission
summary: MeitY launches Chariot-1 AI models under the IndiaAI Mission
detailed: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) launched the Chariot-1 AI model suite under the IndiaAI Mission on November 26, 2026.
Developed by Chariot Artificial Intelligence, the models come in three sizes (745M, 1.7B, and 10.7B parameters) and support English alongside 10 Indian languages for text-to-speech tasks.
The IndiaAI Mission was approved in March 2024 with a five-year outlay of Rs 10,371.92 crore to build indigenous AI capabilities.
This release matters because it aims to reduce dependence on foreign AI platforms by providing sovereign models optimized for India's diverse linguistic landscape.
sentences: India's AI ambitions are getting another homegrown addition, and this one can speak 11 Indian languages.

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has unveiled Chariot-1, a new suite of AI models designed to handle everything from language-based tasks to multilingual speech generation.
Developed by Chariot Artificial Intelligence Pvt.
Ltd., the models were launched at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on 26 November 2026 under the IndiaAI Mission.
The launch was inaugurated by S Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY.
India’s push for homegrown AI has picked its first four teams, with Chariot among those building sovereign models for Indian languages and local needs.
The launch adds another contender to India's growing pool of indigenous AI systems, with a focus on making language models work across the country's diverse linguistic landscape.
Chariot-1 is building out more than a language model.
Its suite also includes a text-to-speech (TTS) model, with both models pre-trained from scratch in India, according to MeitY.
Built to run across different computing setups, Chariot-1 comes in three sizes: 10.7 billion, 1.7 billion and 745 million parameters.
The 11-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model activates 4 billion parameters per token.
Its companion TTS model can generate speech in English and 10 Indian languages: Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, Telugu, Bengali, Odia and Punjabi.
MeitY said the system is designed to handle context while converting numbers, dates, currencies, units, URLs and abbreviations into speech.
These details can be particularly challenging for speech applications dealing with Indian languages.
Chariot is led by co-founders Parth Sarthi and Suvrat Bhooshan.
The launch event also featured a discussion between Bhooshan and Vishal Dhupar, Managing Director, South Asia, NVIDIA, on AI research and the evolving technology landscape.
The launch is part of the government's larger effort to build an indigenous AI ecosystem through the IndiaAI Mission, approved in March 2024 with an outlay of Rs 10,371.92 crore over five years.

Its foundation models pillar supports the development of homegrown large, small and multimodal AI systems trained for India-specific applications, while reducing dependence on externally developed platforms.

MeitY said Chariot's research includes techniques to improve training efficiency and multilingual representation, including methods to reduce token counts for Indian-language text and speed up training.
The reported performance and benchmark figures remain company and ministry claims that will require wider independent evaluation.
Now, the next challenge is making these models accessible.
Licensing terms, availability and large-scale testing will determine whether developers, businesses and public-sector organisations adopt them.
Building an AI model in India is one milestone.
Getting developers and businesses to use it at scale is the real test.
